recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Handle the broader future identifier usage-note linkage under FHIR-48692 or a successor once that work is Applied/Published; do not change FHIR-44644 unless the active Identifier.system comment loses the registry reminder or link.
issue_request: FHIR-44644 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked that Identifier.system more visibly warn that standard identifier-system URIs defined by FHIR, Terminology.hl7.org, and HL7 affiliates SHALL be used for certain identifier types, with a link to identifier-registry.html.
initial_application: Jira-tagged commits 1750c4b0015c3def5b500a3e91c9280c9d2a42f3 and 4aa564f12654dc883112ff56c3b9ca271dea615e, both titled 'FHIR-44644 Identifier.system notes', added and normalized the Identifier.system comment in source/datatypes/identifier.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Identifier as an active datatype and maps default datatype pages to datatypes.html, so source/datatypes/identifier.xml is build-scoped source. Confluence PA and FHIR-I records support the same concern: identifier-registry.html was too hidden, and FHIR-I voted FHIR-44644 Persuasive with Mod 11-0-0 on 2024-05-13. Later FHIR-48692 is related broader identifier-usage work but remains Resolved - change required and does not supersede this seed wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Identifier.system comment already says that the FHIR specification, terminology.hl7.org, and HL7 affiliates define identifier systems that SHALL be used for certain types of identifiers, and it links to identifier-registry.html for specific rules.

related_jiras.note: Earlier PA identifier question that now points to FHIR-44644 as one of the core-spec follow-up tickets.
Broader identifier guidance issue, Resolved - change required, with pattern-note changes and remaining identifier-element link work outside this seed scope.
Older published Patient identifier-allocation guidance referenced from the same PA identifier discussion trail but not determinative for Identifier.system.
